training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.rationale: Training is a job that exits; serving is a process that must stay up. They differ in resource shape (a fit spikes memory, an inference does not), in scaling (train scales to zero, serving needs a warm replica), and in failure handling (a job retries, a service must stay available). Running a fit inside the serving process couples them at the worst point: the fit's memory spike is charged to the same cgroup as the live model cache, so a retrain can OOM-kill the endpoint that is currently answering. The trainer image also carries fit-time dependencies a serving process never calls, which is dead weight on every cold start.
training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.consequence: POST /retrain never fits anything itself. It records intent and returns; the existing trainer image does the work, spawned the same way MODEL-FLOW-003-T04 already spawns it.
training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.scope_correction: NARROWED 2026-08-25. This decision remains right for a long-running synchronous serving process (MODEL-SERVE-002) and for never fitting inside one. It was over-applied when written: it was read as 'inference always needs its own image', and scheduled batch inference is a counterexample its own rationale does not cover. See short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference. MODEL-SERVE-002-T01 (a separate serving image) is unaffected and stays.

deploy_is_a_row_change_not_an_image_buil.chosen: One generic serving image; the production pointer lives in Postgres
deploy_is_a_row_change_not_an_image_buil.rationale: The alternative — one image per model — makes every retrain a CI run and every rollback a redeploy, and turns N models into N deployments to operate. Since the model is data the process loads, not code it links against, the version in production is a fact about a row. Promotion becomes an UPDATE and rollback becomes the same UPDATE in reverse, which is what makes rollback fast enough to actually use during an incident.

rejected.One container per model: Isolates dependencies perfectly and keeps the blast radius to one model, which is the right call ONLY if models genuinely disagree about their dependencies. Revisit per FRAMEWORK, not per model: if MODEL-FLOW-009 lands and brings torch or tensorflow into the picture, a second serving image for sequence models is justified where a second image per tabular model is not.
rejected.A mutable latest/ key in MinIO: Rejected for the reason MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 already gives on the training side: overwriting an object destroys the thing you roll back TO. It also cannot be read consistently — two replicas can observe different bytes behind one key with no way to tell.

ORIGINAL NOTE, PRESERVED: 'Training today spawns containers against a Docker daemon and tracks them with an in-memory watch() (trainning-container.authorized.service.ts). OPTIONS, not yet chosen: (a) keep the Docker-daemon spawn and give serving its own supervisor with boot reconciliation; (b) run serving as an ordinary long-lived service...; (c) an external orchestrator... DECIDE BEFORE MODEL-SERVE-002.'

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T05): the premise is stale. MODEL-FLOW-011-T04 — the reconciliation this decision said was only 'opened' — is now COMPLETED. Read from trainning-container.authorized.service.ts:53-123: `onModuleInit` calls `reconcileOrphanedRuns()`, which walks every RUNNING row against the Docker daemon's own state and either marks it FAILED (container gone), marks it based on actual exit (container finished while the process was down), or RE-ATTACHES `watch()` to a container still alive. The stated objection to option (a) no longer holds.

RESOLUTION IS A NARROWING, NOT A full decision: for MODEL-SERVE-006 (short-lived infer.py containers, per decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference), CHOSEN: option (a), the existing Docker-daemon spawn — now verified adequate by the landed reconciliation. Short-lived containers exit and get reaped every run; there is no long-lived state for a restart to strand beyond what reconciliation already covers. For MODEL-SERVE-002 (a genuinely long-running synchronous serving process), this STAYS OPEN — nothing read in this audit pass decides it, and MODEL-SERVE-006 does not depend on it (see MODEL-SERVE-006's own dependency_notes.MODEL-SERVE-002: 'NOT a dependency, deliberately').

short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.chosen: Short-lived containers on the existing trainer image, second entrypoint
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.rationale: REVISES the scope of training_and_serving_are_separate_planes rather than contradicting it. That decision's reason is specific: a FIT spikes memory and, sharing a cgroup with a long-running cache, can OOM-kill the endpoint currently answering. Hourly batch inference is not a long-running process and holds no cache, so that reason does not apply to it. What is left is a comparison the existing code wins outright — trainning-container.authorized.service.ts already spawns, resource-limits and reaps containers; ModelTrainingRunLog and the /log callback already give per-run logs; image_digest provenance already comes for free. A second entrypoint (infer.py) beside train.py in images/trainer/ reuses all of it. Cold start is a python import, 3-5s, which is noise at a one-hour cadence.
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.consequence: MODEL-SERVE-006 needs no serving process, no cache-invalidation-on-promote, and no readiness protocol. Those belong to MODEL-SERVE-002 (synchronous /predict) alone, which is a SEPARATE requirement arriving later — do not build a serving service in order to get an hourly run.
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.also: One image, not two, additionally removes a divergence risk the two-image plan created: both entrypoints unpickle the same model.joblib, so they cannot disagree about the library that wrote it.

metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.chosen: predictions.parquet is the source of truth; metrics.json is a cache
metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.rationale: The alternative — the client sends a metric set and the container computes exactly those — has one failure that gets worse over time: adding a metric next month leaves every existing run without it, so a comparison table shows a column of em-dashes, and the only way to fill it is to RETRAIN models in order to compute a number that never needed a fit. Deriving from the stored predictions instead means a new metric is recomputable across all history, and the same definitions serve both evaluation (test-split predictions) and monitoring (inference predictions) — one implementation, so 'r2 at training' and 'r2 in monitoring' cannot drift into two numbers that look comparable and are not.
metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.constraint: STATE THE BOUNDARY EXPLICITLY IN THE REGISTRY. Only metrics computable from (actual, predicted) plus scalars already in run_manifest.json (e.g. feature_count for adjusted R²) are backfillable. Anything needing feature values, residual-vs-feature structure or model internals is NOT, and must be marked so — otherwise the registry mixes metrics that can be added retroactively with metrics that cannot, in one table, and nobody can tell which is which.

open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_byt.note: OPENED 2026-09-01 BY MODEL-SERVE-000-T07, RESOLVED 2026-09-01 BY MODEL-SERVE-001-T01. ORIGINAL, PRESERVED: 'NEW 2026-09-01, OPENED BY MODEL-SERVE-000-T07, NOT RESOLVED HERE — an audit surfaces the tension, MODEL-SERVE-001 decides it. MODEL-SERVE-000-T07's own detail forbids fixing the feature-spec-retention gap by copying feature_spec.json into the run prefix... But DS-LAKE-025's `adopt_artifact`... is live, working precedent for the OPPOSITE principle... Both are correct in their own scope and they point opposite directions on the same question.'
open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_byt.rationale: The two precedents are not actually in tension once the difference in what each one is protecting is named. DS-LAKE-025 copies bytes OUT OF `drafts/` because the SOURCE prefix (a DatasetDraft's own workspace) is reclaimable — a dataset draft's sweeper can and does delete `drafts/{draftId}/...` once abandoned, so the saved Dataset must own independent bytes or a later reclaim takes it down. MODEL-SERVE-000-T07 measured the opposite fact for models: the FINAL artifact every run trains against is ALREADY unconditionally excluded from the cleanup candidate query (`artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts`'s `where: { type: { not: 'FINAL' } }`), and an adopted run's own prefix (`drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/...`) is protected by MODEL-FLOW-011-T05's adopted-run guard. There is no reclaimable source for a copy to protect against — copying would duplicate storage against a risk that does not exist, and it would violate MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's adopt-by-pointer rule for the same reason that rule exists on the training side: the row records what happened, it is not a workspace, and a copy is a second, driftable copy of facts the run row already owns.

rejected.Copy goldObjectKey/model.joblib/feature_: Rejected per the rationale above — no reclaimable source exists for models the way `drafts/{draftId}/artifacts/...` is reclaimable for an abandoned DatasetDraft, so the DS-LAKE-025 justification does not transfer. Revisit ONLY if a future change makes FINAL artifacts or adopted-run prefixes reclaimable while a ModelVersion still references them — at which point this decision inherits DS-LAKE-025's own reasoning instead of contradicting it.

open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_byt.implementation: `ModelVersion.goldArtifactId/goldObjectKey/artifactChecksum/featureSpecKey/modelObjectKey` are copied as STRING KEYS from `ModelTrainingRun`'s own pinned columns at version-creation time (one hop, per MODEL-SERVE-000-T03/T07) — the row never re-derives through the dataset's current artifact, and it never fetches or duplicates the underlying bytes.

serving_transform_is_an_extracted_module.chosen: Extract to_model_ready + _scale_column + assert_scaling_coverage into a shared package (softsensor_scaling, packages/py-scaling/); apps/python switches to the extracted copy in the same change
serving_transform_is_an_extracted_module.rationale: MODEL-SERVE-002-T05's own audit answer was 'call it, no extraction needed' — correct as far as it went, but written before this ledger settled WHERE serving runs. apps/python is the only process that currently imports to_model_ready, and apps/python carries no scikit-learn/joblib (confirmed: zero executable references anywhere in the tree). With serving in a separate apps/serving process (per serving_host_undecided's resolution), 'call it' is not reachable — there is no shared process to call into. T05's own text anticipates exactly this fork: 'If the path is callable, call it. If it is not, extract it into a module BOTH the trainer and the server import, and make the trainer use the extracted copy in the same change.' Two importers now exist (apps/python, apps/serving), so the second clause is the one that applies.

rejected.Duplicate to_model_ready into apps/servi: Rejected outright — this is precisely the drift T05's own text warns against ('leaving the trainer on the original and the server on a copy... would pass every test written against either side alone'). A second implementation of the empty-scaling-array default lookup (scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER)) is the exact failure mode MODEL-SERVE-000-T03's empty-scaling finding describes.

serving_transform_is_an_extracted_module.constraint: Import direction is one-way: softsensor_scaling depends on pandas/numpy only; apps/python's object_store.py/cleaning_service.py import FROM it and re-export the moved names so every existing caller keeps working unchanged. Nothing in the package may import back from intergrations.* or services.* — object_store.py is imported by every router in apps/python, so a back-reference is a circular import that fails at process startup.

serving_cache_staleness_bound.rationale: MODEL-SERVE-002-T07's own text: 'state the maximum time a promoted version can take to become live, and make it a number someone chose rather than an emergent property.' 30s is short enough that an operator promoting during an incident does not perceive a hung rollout, and long enough that the descriptor endpoint (one DB read + two python round trips) is not re-hit on every request. Applies to the descriptor TTL cache in apps/serving/services/descriptor.py; the bound is the TTL plus the duration of requests already in flight when a promote lands, per T07's own framing.
serving_cache_staleness_bound.verification: MODEL-SERVE-002-V02 promotes under continuous /predict load and asserts every response is answerable by some valid version with the switchover landing inside this bound.

batch_worker_is_a_trainer_image_mode.chosen: A new MODE=batch on the existing images/trainer/ image — a short-lived container, not the apps/serving process.
batch_worker_is_a_trainer_image_mode.rationale: Decided WITH THE USER before implementation. Matches decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference's own reasoning: a batch score is not a long-running process and holds no cache, so training_and_serving_are_separate_planes's OOM-kill-the-live-endpoint concern does not apply to it. The container gets the strongest available memory isolation (its own 8GiB cgroup cap, ReadonlyRootfs, tmpfs /scratch) rather than sharing a cgroup with apps/serving's live model LRU cache. It also reuses, rather than reinvents, everything trainning-container.authorized.service.ts already provides: spawn/watch/reap, per-row reconcileOrphanedRuns()-style restart recovery, resource limits, and image_digest provenance.

rejected.apps/serving file-scoring endpoint: Rejected: a batch score run inside the serving process is charged to the SAME cgroup as the live model cache MODEL-SERVE-002 built — a wide batch input can pressure memory the same way a fit does, which is the exact coupling training_and_serving_are_separate_planes exists to prevent, just moved one layer down. It would also need the serving process to hold job state, and it is deliberately credential-free (no DB, no S3 creds) — confirmed live: apps/serving/requirements.txt has no psycopg/minio/boto3/prisma.
rejected.backend chunks into the existing synchro: Rejected: N HTTP round trips per batch (one per SERVING_MAX_ROWS-sized chunk), still loads the live serving process anyway, and requires apps/backend (Node) to read and write parquet, which no code in this repo does today. Output assembly in Node is also exactly the memory risk T03 warns about, moved into the wrong process.

batch_worker_is_a_trainer_image_mode.cost_accepted: images/trainer/ cannot apply the training-time scaling transform today (no to_model_ready, no softsensor_scaling — confirmed live, zero matches). Its build context is images/trainer/ only. This decision requires adding the extracted package as a dependency AND moving that build context to the repo root, mirroring the move apps/serving/Dockerfile already made for the same reason. Checked before accepting this cost: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile (docs/feature_list.json:179, verified verbatim), so the move breaks no pipeline — only the manual build command changes.

batch_input_is_pre_scale.chosen: The batch input parquet carries the model's feature columns in raw engineering units — the identical contract MODEL-SERVE-002's synchronous /predict already uses. The worker applies the fitted scaling transform (softsensor_scaling.to_model_ready) before predicting.
batch_input_is_pre_scale.rationale: Decided WITH THE USER. One request contract for both the synchronous and batch paths, rather than two. Critically avoids the silent-wrong-answer trap this ledger repeatedly guards against (the empty-scaling-array trap, MODEL-SERVE-000-T03's highest-severity finding): under this contract, supplying raw values is the CORRECT thing to do, not a mistake that produces a plausible wrong number with no error. The rejected alternative (an already-scaled, GOLD-shaped input) would make the batch contract differ from /predict's for the same model and would require the caller to obtain scalingParams themselves to pre-scale it — reintroducing exactly the class of silent failure MODEL-SERVE-002-T05 was built to close.
batch_input_is_pre_scale.consequence: pipelines/batch.py must call softsensor_scaling.assert_scaling_coverage before transforming, the same guard rows_to_predictions applies in apps/serving/services/predict.py — one shared function, not two implementations that could drift.

ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_.chosen: Ground truth arrives by RE-FETCHING THE TARGET TAG from the window's own source on a second, much longer lag (InferenceSchedule.truthLagMinutes), joined to the window's stored predictions.parquet on a stated tolerance. No CSV-upload surface is built.
ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_.provenance: Decided AT PLAN APPROVAL on 2026-09-14, from a written plan carrying the evidence below. Recorded this precisely rather than as 'decided with the user before the pass began' — this ledger treats that phrase as a load-bearing provenance claim that later passes cite, so it is not applied to a conversation that did not happen.
ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_.rationale: The target IS a tag on the same historian, not an artifact a human uploads: a real run's feature_spec.json records target_y=S204FBP.lab, and FeaturePreset.targetY's own schema comment states 'The lab measurement this preset predicts. Always a `.lab` tag.' MODEL-SERVE-006-T04's own detail already routed this here — 'The lab target's own latency is a different and much longer number and belongs to T08, not here — inference needs features only' — and T08 then landed evaluation-only, naming T03 as the holder of the monitoring half. Everything the fetch needs is already persisted per model (InferenceSchedule.sourceId + fetchConfig), the target column is already resolved and exposed as descriptor.targetY (ModelVersion -> sourceRun -> ModelTrainingRun.targetY), and apps/python's materialize_window already fetches an arbitrary tag list over an arbitrary past range from either PI or SQL. So the truth fetch is the SAME call this system already makes, with a one-element tag list and a longer lag — no new ingestion surface, no new connector, no manual step per join.

rejected.Persist the evaluation UI's lab points /: Viable and NOT ruled out forever — a general multipart path already exists and is proven end-to-end (@fastify/multipart in main.ts, FastAPI UploadFile, the feature-preset .xlsx import). Rejected FOR THIS PASS because it needs a new endpoint, a new Prisma table and a human step per join to reproduce information the historian already holds. Reconsider only if lab results turn out never to reach the historian.
rejected.Both paths in one pass: Roughly doubles the surface for one shared join/metric half. The upload path can be added later against the same InferenceWindowTruth rows without reworking this one.

ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_.granularity: PAIRS, with metrics rolled over a set of pairs — not a per-window metric. Lab truth arrives hours or days apart while predictions are per-interval, so most windows hold ZERO lab samples and some exactly one. A per-window RMSE computed over one sample is a single residual wearing a metric's name, which is the plausible-wrong-answer failure this ledger's own global_definition_of_done forbids. Each row therefore stores SUFFICIENT STATISTICS (n, sumSe, sumAe, sumSigned, sumActual, sumActualSq), the same trick poolFeatureStats already uses for drift, so a rolling metric over N windows is exact and a future registry metric is backfillable without re-fetching truth.
ground_truth_arrives_by_re_fetching_the_.consequence: A truth value must be EVIDENCED BY AN ACTUAL LAB EVENT in the interval, never by a held or interpolated summary. The live PI path is a TimeWeighted/Average summary (PIWebAPI.getAverageValue -> streamSet.get_summaries_ad_hoc) and PI holds a sparse .lab tag's last value between samples, so inheriting the schedule's own fetchConfig summary settings would return a plausible number for EVERY interval — including every interval with no lab event at all — and publish a confident R2 computed against a held value. The truth fetch therefore overrides those settings rather than copying them.

findings: CORRECTED 2026-08-24 FROM A MINIO SCREENSHOT OF A REAL RUN (bucket `datasets`, key drafts/1ce30923-394b-4135-b324-0e913606dcf9/runs/61f9aa28-0c31-4e99-bd52-4674200f72f6/, timestamps 2026-08-19 11:44 — one of the two runs MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 live-verified). The prior finding called the run's descriptor `manifest.json`; the object is `run_manifest.json`. The rename is not cosmetic: the name scopes it to the RUN, and a run descriptor and a serving descriptor are not the same document. A run manifest records what happened during a fit; serving needs what is required to LOAD the result. They may overlap, but assuming they are identical is exactly the kind of assumption MODEL-SERVE-000 exists to stop. Contents remain UNVERIFIED — the screenshot shows names and sizes only.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03). ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NEW AND HIGHEST SEVERITY IN THIS LEDGER — THE RUN DIRECTORY IS NOT A SELF-CONTAINED SERVING BUNDLE, CONFIRMED BY OBSERVATION. The directory holds exactly four objects: metrics.json (155 B), model.joblib (1.1 KiB), predictions.parquet (24.9 KiB), run_manifest.json (1.2 KiB). There is NO feature_spec.json and NO scaler or preprocessor object. model.joblib at 1.1 KiB is corroborating evidence rather than proof, but it is strong: a fitted sklearn Pipeline carrying a scaler's own state does not serialise to a kilobyte — this is an estimator alone. So a serving process cannot open this prefix and predict. It must resolve Model -> ModelTrainingRun -> DatasetArtifact.featureSpecKey -> feature_spec.json, three hops across two entities, and the transform state (scalers, the effective column list from select_columns + force_keep_target) lives at the far end of that chain on an entity the USER CAN EDIT.' THE 'THREE HOPS' CLAIM IS WRONG — read from packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma:1006-1031: ModelTrainingRun carries goldArtifactId, goldObjectKey, artifactChecksum AND featureSpecKey directly on the run row, set at launch from the ARTIFACT the run was actually created against (model-run-launch.authorized.service.ts:126, `featureSpecKey: artifact.featureSpecKey`) — never re-derived through the dataset's current artifact. Verified against the live dev database: 0 of 73 ModelTrainingRun rows have a null featureSpecKey. So this is ONE hop off the run row (ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey -> feature_spec.json), not three hops through an editable dataset. The 'not co-located, so a correct implementation can still be fed the wrong spec' exposure the finding worried about does not exist: the pinned key cannot silently repoint to an edited dataset's current artifact.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T07). ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NEW — NOTHING PINS OR PROTECTS THE ARTIFACT A MODEL WAS FITTED AGAINST. MODEL-FLOW-010's own finding states that editing a dataset keeps the Dataset id and moves currentArtifactId, and correctly concludes that ModelDraft.datasetId stays valid. That conclusion is right for the WIZARD and wrong to inherit here: a served model needs the SPECIFIC artifact it was fitted against, not the dataset's current one, and neither ledger says that artifact is retained for as long as a model references it. Two separate objects can therefore be reclaimed out from under one production model — its bytes (guarded upstream by MODEL-FLOW-011-T05) and its feature spec (guarded by nothing). Losing either is the same outage.' WRONG ON BOTH CLAUSES, verified against schema.prisma and the live dev DB/MinIO. PINNING: ModelTrainingRun already carries goldArtifactId, goldObjectKey, artifactChecksum and featureSpecKey — an id-only reference was never the design (see schema.prisma:1019-1031's own comment: 'NOT how the container resolves data ... an id-only reference would silently retrain on different rows later'). PROTECTION: measured live — ALL 73 ModelTrainingRun rows train against a FINAL artifact, zero against GOLD. `artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts`'s candidate query (`where: { type: { not: 'FINAL' } }`) and `artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts:236` (`if (artifact.type === 'FINAL') continue`) both exclude FINAL unconditionally — it is never a cleanup candidate. Post-DS-LAKE-025, FINAL owns its bytes outright at `{datasetId}/artifacts/{artifactId}/` with feature_spec.json copied alongside (`adopt_artifact`, artifact_service.py:1268). 0 of 61 SUCCEEDED runs point at a missing or objectReclaimedAt-stamped artifact (measured). TWO REAL EXPOSURES SURVIVE, NEITHER THE ONE ORIGINALLY CLAIMED: (1) the FINAL protection is a TYPE EXCLUSION, not a ModelTrainingRun reference check — nothing but PreprocessingJob (QUEUED/RUNNING) counts as a live reference in the cleanup sweep, and `artifact-cleanup-eligibility.ts:314-324` explicitly allows GOLD/SILVER to age out 'even if still lineage-reachable', reasoning that an unreached one is storage 'nothing can ever reclaim and nothing reads' — false the moment a ModelTrainingRun points at it, which no launch path currently forbids. Latent, not live, today. (2) `deleteDatasetService` (apps/backend/src/api/v1/dataset/authorized/dataset.authorized.service.ts:234-246) checks ownership only, then `prisma.dataset.delete` — Dataset cascades onto DatasetArtifact (schema.prisma:563), and ModelTrainingRun.goldArtifactId is a bare String with no FK, so it dangles silently. Bytes still resolve (goldObjectKey/featureSpecKey are pinned keys, not FKs), but the objects become permanently unreclaimable — cleanup enumerates DatasetArtifact rows, and the row is gone. UPSTREAM TICKETS NAMED, NOT WRITTEN HERE: deleteDatasetService should refuse or warn when a ModelTrainingRun references the dataset's artifacts; the cleanup sweep's live-reference set should include ModelTrainingRun.goldArtifactId before any launch path can target a non-FINAL artifact.

NEW — ONE BUCKET HOLDS EVERYTHING. Model run outputs live in the `datasets` bucket (17.4 MiB / 138 objects at the time of the screenshot). That is fine today and cheap to leave alone, but it means no bucket-scoped lifecycle rule, retention policy or access grant can distinguish a production model's bytes from an abandoned dataset draft's. Anyone who later writes a lifecycle rule intending it for datasets writes it for models too. Record it now so that decision is made deliberately rather than discovered.

NEW AND USEFUL — MODEL-SERVE-002-V01 IS RUNNABLE TODAY. predictions.parquet exists in the run directory (24.9 KiB), so the no-skew test — score a row from the model's own test split through the live endpoint and assert it matches the recorded prediction — has real reference data against a real fitted model, with no live wizard and no MODEL-FLOW-007 required. This is the one verification in this ledger that can be built before its own dependencies land, and it is also the most load-bearing.

NEW — NO CHECKSUM SIDECAR EXISTS. There is no .sha256 or equivalent object beside model.joblib, so a checksum either lives inside run_manifest.json or is not computed at all. MODEL-SERVE-000-T01 must distinguish those two, because they lead to different work: reading a field, versus adding a write to the trainer AND accepting that every artifact predating that change has no checksum and needs a stated policy.

CONFIRMED 2026-08-24 by reading run_manifest.json from the run in the screenshot. The prior finding, and MODEL-SERVE-000-T01's three questions, are now answered and the finding is REPLACED rather than deleted so the audit trail survives: (1) a checksum EXISTS — model_sha256, plus artifact_checksum for the GOLD parquet; (2) provenance is pinned by image_digest (scgc/soft-sensor-trainer@sha256:…), which is STRONGER than the sklearn/joblib version string this ledger asked for, because it pins the whole runtime rather than one library; (3) the manifest does NOT carry a featureSpecKey, but it DOES inline feature_columns, target_y, target_scaled and derived_from_target — four of the fields serving would otherwise have walked to the spec for. seed and the full split record (method, ratio, cut_timestamp, labelled/train/test rows) are also present. This manifest is materially better than this ledger assumed, and the earlier UNVERIFIED framing overstated the gap.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03), PREMISE INVERTED. ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NARROWED 2026-08-24 — THE ONLY MISSING SERVING INPUT IS SCALER STATE. With feature_columns inlined, the three-hop chain to feature_spec.json collapses to one open question rather than a general dependency: where does a run's SCALER configuration live, and is it recoverable at serve time? The manifest records target_scaled: false, which proves the system tracks scaling on the target side, and records nothing about the feature side. model.joblib at 1.1 KiB for a bare 8-feature OLS is consistent with this particular run having no scalers at all — which is why it cannot answer the question. MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 must therefore be run against a run that DID scale, not this one; the smallest, cleanest artifact is the least informative one here.' SCALER STATE IS NOT MISSING. feature_spec.json carries `scalingParams` — the actual FITTED params per tag (e.g. `{"TI-101": {"min": 70.0, "max": 75.0}}`), written by artifact_service.features() / feature_spec_service.py:241. ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey pins the exact spec (schema.prisma:1031), verified non-null on 73/73 runs. The primitive that applies a FITTED transform to new rows without re-fitting already exists and is tested: `to_model_ready(frame, tags, scalers, fitted_params=scaling_params)`, wrapped by `prepare_holdout_for_run`/`replay_holdout_for_run` (artifact_service.py:570-706), which already REFUSES when a tag would scale without a recorded scalingParams entry (artifact_service.py:676-687) rather than silently re-fitting. Serving's answer to 'call it or extract it' (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03's own question) is CALL IT — these entry points are object-storage-keyed (`store.get_frame(source_key)`), which fits MODEL-SERVE-006's parquet windows directly; a synchronous row-list /predict needs a thin in-memory wrapper, not an extraction. WHY THE ORIGINAL INFERENCE FAILED: the run examined had `target_scaled: false` and a 1.1 KiB model.joblib, read as 'no scalers at all'. Both premises are true and the conclusion is false — feature_spec_service.py:250 sets `target_scaled` from `scalers.get(target_y, "none")` (the TARGET defaults to none), while feature_service.py:79 sets `DEFAULT_SCALER = "minmax"` (FEATURES default to minmax). Two different defaults in one document. The joblib is small because scalers were never in the pickle — they live in the spec, not the model object. See the new empty-`scaling` finding below for the trap this created.

NEW 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03), HIGHEST-SEVERITY FINDING OF THIS AUDIT PASS — THE EMPTY-`scaling` TRAP. feature_service.py:79 sets `DEFAULT_SCALER = "minmax"`. feature_spec_service.py's `scaling` array (line ~23) holds one `{tag, method}` entry ONLY for a tag with an EXPLICIT scaler choice — a tag left at the default writes NOTHING to `scaling`, even though it IS scaled. Measured directly against all 21 `feature_spec.json` objects currently in MinIO: every single one has `len(scaling) == 0` while `len(scalingParams) == 22`. So on every real dataset in this system, every tag is minmax-scaled by default, and `scaling: []` is exactly what that looks like on disk — indistinguishable, by that field alone, from 'nothing was scaled'. A serving process that reads `scaling` to decide whether to transform inputs, finds it empty, and concludes no scaling is needed will feed RAW values into a model fitted on SCALED inputs and return a plausible wrong number — silently, with no error, no missing field, nothing to alert on. The existing preprocessing code is safe today only because `to_model_ready` reads `scalers.get(tag, DEFAULT_SCALER)`, never `scaling` directly. Any new serving code (MODEL-SERVE-002-T05, MODEL-SERVE-006-T03) MUST resolve each tag's scaler the same way — from `scalingParams`' keys and/or the same default-aware lookup — never by branching on whether `scaling` is non-empty.

NEW 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T04) — SERVABILITY CENSUS AGAINST LIVE DATA. Read all 21 `feature_spec.json` objects in MinIO and cross-referenced against the live dev Postgres: 0 of 21 specs have a non-empty `derived_from_target` (the target-history request-contract fork in MODEL-SERVE-002-T06 guards a class the schema permits but no real spec currently uses); 0 of 21 have `target_scaled: true`; exactly 1 of 21 has zero `scalingParams` entries and is therefore UNSERVABLE without re-fitting — and it is `drafts/c47bfa69-.../artifacts/b9e25f8d-.../feature_spec.json`, the exact artifact this ledger's own MinIO screenshot and repeated findings are built from (it predates DS-LAKE-018-T02, so it has no recorded fitted params). The coverage guard in `prepare_holdout_for_run` (artifact_service.py:676-687) already refuses to serve it rather than silently re-fitting, which is the correct behaviour. Of 73 ModelTrainingRun rows, 0 have a null `featureSpecKey`, and 61 SUCCEEDED. This ledger's most-cited example run is its ONLY unservable one, which is worth knowing before anyone scopes MODEL-SERVE-002 against it as a representative case.

IMAGE_DIGEST CREATES A NEW RETENTION DEPENDENCY. Pinning by digest is the right call, but a digest pins nothing once the image is garbage-collected from the registry — at which point the ONLY record of the runtime a production model was fitted under is a string that resolves to nothing. Whatever retains the model object and its artifact must extend to the trainer image any live ModelVersion names. This dependency did not exist under the version-string approach this ledger originally proposed; it is a consequence of the better mechanism, not a defect in it.

CORRECTED 2026-09-01 (MODEL-SERVE-000-T06). ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NEW — `drafts/` IS A SHARED ROOT FOR TWO UNRELATED ENTITIES IN ONE BUCKET. Observed directly: the run lives at drafts/1ce30923-…/runs/… (a ModelDraft) while its gold_object_key reads drafts/c47bfa69-…/artifacts/… (a DatasetDraft). Same bucket, same first segment, different tables, different lifecycles, different sweepers... The exposure is in the SWEEPERS... it is UNVERIFIED whether [DS-LAKE-014's DatasetDraft sweeper] reclaims by structural predicate or by a drafts/{id}/ prefix. If the latter, a dataset sweep can reach a model draft's prefix.' NOT REAL, confirmed by reading both call paths. DS-LAKE-014's sweeper (artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts:270-273) calls Python's `/v1/preprocess/artifacts/reclaim` with `{ object_key: artifact.objectKey }` — the specific DatasetArtifact row's own key — which resolves via `reclaim_artifact` -> `split_data_key(object_key)` to that artifact's own `.../artifacts/{artifactId}/` prefix (artifact_service.py:1213-1236). This is a DIFFERENT endpoint from the model side's `/v1/preprocess/models/runs/reclaim` -> `reclaim_draft_runs`, which independently scopes to `drafts/{draftId}/runs/[{runId}/]` (artifact_service.py:1241-1264) and never a bare `drafts/{draftId}/`. Neither sweeper derives its prefix from a shared or naive draftId-only guess; each is keyed off its own row's structural data. No upstream ticket needed.

NEW — NOTHING GATES PROMOTION ON WHETHER THE MODEL IS ANY GOOD. The observed run has r2 = -2.4068: worse than predicting the mean, i.e. no predictive value. Every claim made about it is nonetheless true — MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 correctly recorded it as SUCCEEDED with real metrics, and the leakage guard correctly found nothing to check (derived_from_target is empty, so there is no leakage; the model is simply bad). MODEL-FLOW-000-T02 hardened this codebase against an implausibly HIGH R², and this is the opposite direction, which no criterion in either ledger covers. MODEL-SERVE-001-T05 refuses a version whose artifact cannot be LOADED; it says nothing about one that loads fine and is useless. See MODEL-SERVE-001-T06.

ORIGINAL CLAIM, PRESERVED: 'NEW 2026-08-25 — CHANGE THE EVALUATION METRICS FROM THE UI IS NOT REACHABLE FROM WHERE THE UI IS TODAY... mpSelectedMetricsAtom currently filters browser-computed values, so pointing it at a registry while phase-3-evaluation.tsx still calls computeFit produces a prettier filter over the wrong numbers. NEW 2026-08-25 — THE WIZARD'S OWN GATE IS LOOSER THAN THE RUN-CREATION GUARD BEHIND IT. phase-2-training-config.tsx computes `canTrain = targetVariables.length > 0 && training.status !== 'training' && tags.length > 0`, and renders AutoMlToggles as freely operable. MODEL-FLOW-003-T10 established that use-model-training refuses anything other than exactly one target, exactly one algorithm, and AutoML off. ALSO NOT IN THE ORIGINAL LEDGER: Model.data.deployStatus (written only by phase-6-deploy.tsx:113, apps/client/app/(default)/models/create/components/pipeline/phase-6-deploy.tsx) has zero backend semantics — it lives inside an untyped Json? column nothing server-side reads. /predict resolves ModelVersion.stage = 'PRODUCTION' only and must ignore deployStatus entirely; the two notions of 'deployed' are unconnected until MODEL-SERVE-006-T12 derives one from the other.

NEW 2026-09-02, LIVE-VERIFIED AGAINST REAL MINIO — GOLD IS ALREADY SCALED; SILVER IS THE PRE-SCALE ARTIFACT. Planning MODEL-SERVE-002-V01 assumed GOLD (post-features, pre-scale) was the right source for pre-scaling feature values to send through /predict. Fetched real objects to check: artifact_service.py's features() applies to_model_ready scaling INTO GOLD ITSELF when request.scale is true (artifact_service.py:792) — GOLD is the fully feature-engineered AND scaled frame; FINAL is an adopted copy of the same bytes (same data_gold.parquet filename, different artifact id/prefix). Verified on run cd2db914-3bb4-4abb-a305-9f3ae19eb50d's lineage: SILVER artifact a61abaf5-4545-4215-a707-aaf6bf843918's FI001.PV at 2026-02-18 15:20:00 is 200.232742 (raw engineering units); GOLD artifact 839570c8-c246-4260-a511-dc2b3a840bd9's FI001.PV at the same timestamp is 0.76 (minmax-scaled), consistent with a scalingParams entry. SILVER also already carries every DERIVED column (Spgr_in_feed_Header_1, Reflux_ratio_per_total_feed_of_Quench_oil_tower confirmed present in SILVER, not just GOLD) — exactly the '/predict's feature columns, pre-scaling' request contract this feature needs, with no inversion required. This run's feature_spec.json also lived the empty-scaling-array trap for real: target_y=S204FBP.lab, target_scaled=false, scaling=[] with scalingParams holding 22 entries.

NEW 2026-09-02, LIVE-VERIFIED — A CV RUN'S predictions.parquet DOES NOT LAND INSIDE ITS OWN GOLD/SILVER RANGE. Run f8ec969e-f13a-4176-8990-ad59b17fd457 (cvFoldsKey set, a cv_expanding run) has predictions.parquet timestamps starting 2026-01-27 00:00:00, which falls inside a real 4-day gap in its GOLD/SILVER timestamp grid (verified: the grid jumps from 2026-01-26 23:55:00 directly to +4 days +10 minutes). This is because a CV run's holdout score comes from score.py's REPLAYED holdout frame (MODEL-FLOW-016-T07), a different object entirely from the GOLD/SILVER the fold training used — never the GOLD/SILVER lineage. MODEL-SERVE-002-V01 must select a non-CV (cvFoldsKey IS NULL) run specifically, not merely any SUCCEEDED run with scalingParams, or its own timestamp lookup silently fails to find a source row.

NEW 2026-09-02, DEV-ENVIRONMENT-ONLY, RECORDED BECAUSE IT COST REAL TIME TWICE — apps/python's presigned URLs default to S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT=http://host.docker.internal:9000, unresolvable when apps/serving runs directly on the host Mac (not in a container) during local live verification. Hit during both V01 and V04: each required restarting apps/python with S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:9000 for the test, then restarting it back to normal afterward, PLUS restarting apps/serving fresh so its 30s descriptor-cache TTL wouldn't keep serving the stale (broken) presigned URL. Separately, a uvicorn --reload process survives a `pkill -f` pattern that omits the literal `--reload` substring (it breaks contiguous matching) — a stale, differently-cached process kept answering on the same port after an intended restart, which is what actually caused the first V04 attempt to look like a false pass. Not a code defect — both are pure dev-workflow hazards worth a line so the next person doesn't re-discover them: kill by exact PID (from `ps aux`), never by a pattern that might not match `--reload`'s insertion point; and any live test through apps/serving from the bare host needs the localhost override for the duration of the test only.

NEW 2026-09-02, LIVE-FOUND, FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE — apps/serving/services/loader.py's `_download` let a `requests` transport failure (e.g. unresolvable host, connection refused) propagate as a raw unhandled exception, reaching the /predict caller as an unmapped HTTP 500 with a leaked stack trace — found by chance when V04's first attempt hit an unresolvable host.docker.internal before the environment override was applied. This directly violated `LoadError`'s own docstring ('safe to surface as a 422, never a bare 500'). Fixed: `_download` now wraps `requests.RequestException` as `LoadError`, which `routers/serve.py` already mapped to 422 (a request-shaped 422 is used deliberately here, consistent with every other LoadError in this codepath, rather than introducing a separate 503-for-transient-failures distinction that no acceptance criterion asks for). Covered by a new unit test using a real unreachable port (127.0.0.1:1), not a mock.

NEW 2026-09-02, LIVE-FOUND — .github/workflows/_build-image.yml's `push:false` MODE WAS UNUSABLE UNTIL NOW, despite being declared in its own input schema (`push: {default: true}`). The 'Build and push' step never set `load:`, so with push:false the built image lands only in the buildx cache — nothing at `steps.ref.outputs.image` for the unconditional Trivy/SBOM steps below it to scan, which would fail on the very first push:false call. Never caught before because every existing caller (release.yml's 3 image jobs, all already broken/unwired for a different reason — the dslake-layout mismatch) uses the push:true default; MODEL-SERVE-002-T01's serving-image.yml is the first real push:false caller. Fixed with one line, `load: ${{ !inputs.push }}` — benefits any future build-and-scan-only caller of this shared workflow, not just serving.

PREMISE CORRECTION 2026-09-02 (MODEL-SERVE-002-T06) — THE SAMPLING-INTERVAL CLAUSE ASKS FOR AN AXIS THIS SYSTEM ALREADY DELIBERATELY REJECTED. T06's ORIGINAL text (2026-08-24, PRESERVED in its `detail`): 'Also validate the submitted history's sampling interval against the spec.' Three facts found by reading the tree, in the ledger's own tradition of each audit correcting its predecessor: (1) `feature_spec.json` RECORDS NO INTERVAL — read the whole of feature_spec_service.build_feature_spec: featureVersion, features, selectedColumns, scaling, scalingParams, encoding, featureHash, target_y, target_scaled, derived_from_target, and nothing else. Prisma has no interval column either (grepped schema.prisma). The interval exists only as a PI-fetch parameter (`summary_duration or '1m'`), never persisted with the artifact. So there is no reference value to validate anything against. (2) THIS REPO ALREADY FACED THE IDENTICAL QUESTION AND ANSWERED IT — artifact_service.py's holdout-replay lead-in check states it outright: 'Computed from the recipe's own compound lookback (max_replay_lookback — a lag on a rolling column compounds), NOT re-derived from a duration/interval a caller would have to look up.' It refuses in ROWS, from the recipe, precisely because an interval is the thing a caller would have to go look up. (3) The primitive already exists and is already proven: `max_replay_lookback`, written for DS-LAKE-018-T04, whose own docstring describes T06's exact failure mode ('null/wrong lag-rolling values ... feed straight into predict(), and depress the metric with no trace of why'). The clause's real defect is that it presumed a request contract that was never built: it assumed /predict would receive target history as a timestamped series, whereas the contract deliberately built passes PRE-COMPUTED feature columns and applies scaling only (the boundary recorded in this feature's own architecture note). Under that contract a lag column is an opaque number whose cadence is unknowable to serving — an interval check could only ever validate a caller's self-declaration, which is an attestation, not a proof. RESOLUTION, taken with the user: retire the interval clause and implement the row-depth guard the precedent already established — serving reports the recipe's compound row depth (via the same shared max_replay_lookback) in its refusal, so a caller learns how far back its history must reach. The alternative considered and rejected as its own future ticket: grow the contract to accept timestamped history and derive the target features in serving — which would require extracting apply_features into the shared package too, since deriving them with a second implementation is exactly the drift T05 exists to prevent. Worth stating plainly for whoever revisits: if that contract is ever built, the interval check becomes both possible AND meaningful, and this clause should be un-retired.

NEW 2026-09-02, LIVE-FOUND AND RESOLVED — TRIVY HARD GATE WOULD HAVE FAILED ON THE FIRST CI RUN. Scanned the real built apps/serving image locally with CI's exact parameters (severity HIGH,CRITICAL, ignore-unfixed) before trusting the workflow to it: 4 HIGH findings. Investigated each rather than blanket-suppressing: `msgpack` (GHSA-6v7p-g79w-8964) and `setuptools` (CVE-2025-47273) are pip's OWN internal vendored copies (confirmed via `pip/_vendor/vendor.txt` inside the built image) — never imported by this repo's code, exercised only inside `pip install` itself, and unfixable from this side since pip 26.2.1 (the latest release at check time) still vendors these exact versions. `lightgbm` (CVE-2024-43598) and `pyarrow` (CVE-2026-25087) are both pinned specifically to match images/trainer/requirements.txt bit-for-bit (the entire reason for T01's separate-image requirement) — bumping either here alone would violate that pin and risk an unverified cross-version pickle roundtrip, a bigger risk than the CVEs' actual exposure (lightgbm's is an RCE via a malicious model file; every model this process loads is checksum-verified against a value read from Postgres, never attacker-supplied). All 4 recorded in .trivyignore with individual dated reasoning (msgpack/setuptools: 2027-03-01, lightgbm/pyarrow: 2026-12-01 — revisit even without an assigned owner). Re-scanned after: exit 0, confirmed live, not assumed.

CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (MODEL-SERVE-003 implementation start) — T04'S 'REUSE presign_artifact' IS RIGHT FOR THE INPUT, WRONG FOR THE OUTPUT. ORIGINAL, PRESERVED: 'Reuse the existing presign path (artifact_service.presign_artifact) rather than writing a second one.' ACTUALLY: presign_artifact (artifact_service.py:1322) refuses anything failing is_committed_artifact_key (object_store.py:1159), which requires BOTH '/artifacts/' in the key AND a filename in ALL_DATA_FILENAMES (:957). A prediction-job output key satisfies neither. The codebase forbids widening that guard in two places (artifact_service.py:1707-1710, schemas/preprocess.py:327-331) and records that this identical mistake already made holdoutMetrics null on 100% of runs — which is precisely why presign_run_object exists as a SECOND function (:1689), for run outputs that are real objects but not committed dataset artifacts either. A prediction-job output is the same shape of problem one level further out. Resolution: reuse presign_artifact to read the INPUT (an existing committed artifact, passes the guard unchanged); add a sibling function for the OUTPUT (prediction_job_key builder + is_prediction_job_key structural guard + presign_prediction_job_object), mirroring exactly how presign_run_object was added.

CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (MODEL-SERVE-003 implementation start) — T01'S VOCABULARY CLAIM IS RIGHT, AND STRONGER THAN STATED; ALSO, ModelFineTuningJob IS DEAD. ORIGINAL, PRESERVED: 'QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELED, mirroring ModelTrainingRun's vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one.' ACTUALLY: FOUR enums already carry this identical five-value set, not one — ModelRunStatus (schema.prisma:1000), PreprocessingJobStatus (:437), LoaderJobStatus (:445), ModelCandidateJobStatus (:1275). LoaderJobStatus's own doc comment states the reason to copy rather than share: 'mirrors PreprocessingJobStatus exactly, so the existing runner patterns (boot sweep, retry, attempt counting) transfer without inventing a second state machine.' PredictionJobStatus is the fifth copy, matching the house one-enum-per-entity convention — Prisma enums are not shared across models in this schema. Also found live: ModelFineTuningJob, which an earlier version of this ledger's own text referenced, no longer exists — it was renamed to ModelCandidateJob in migration 20260827120000_model_flow_013_candidate_job. Do not cite the old name in new work.

CORRECTED 2026-09-02 (MODEL-SERVE-003 implementation start) — T02'S IDEMPOTENCY CLAIM IS CONFIRMED GENUINELY NEW, AND SETTLES WHERE THE KEY LIVES. Searched the whole repo (idempotenc/Idempotency-Key/requestId/dedupe/dedup across apps/backend, apps/python, apps/frontend, apps/serving, packages/prisma): NO idempotency mechanism of any kind exists anywhere in this codebase today. Also checked: @Headers is used in ZERO non-spec backend files (grepped apps/backend/src) — the only inbound headers read anywhere in the backend are user-agent, in two auth controllers. So the idempotency key belongs in the submit endpoint's DTO BODY, not an HTTP header — introducing header-reading here would be the only instance of that pattern in the codebase, which is reason enough to avoid it absent a specific need. The race-safe shape to reuse already exists and is spec-tested, not merely a documented intention: dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts's resolveOrCreateEditDraftService — create, catch P2002 by CONSTRAINT NAME (model-version.authorized.service.ts:76-90's isUniqueViolation(err, constraint) pattern, 'checked by constraint name, not just P2002, so this never masks a genuinely different unique violation'), fall back to reading the winner's row. Tested at dataset-draft.authorized.service.spec.ts:2993 and :3018.

COMPLETED 2026-09-02 (MODEL-SERVE-003) — ALL 5 TASKS + 3 LIVE VERIFICATIONS DONE. Batch prediction ships as MODE=batch on the trainer image (soft-sensor-trainer 1.0.6 — bumped and default-tagged in trainning-container.authorized.service.ts, same discipline as every prior MODE addition: the default image MUST carry the new entrypoint or a job passes validation, spawns, and dies inside the container). images/trainer's own pytest suite (27/27) run for the first time this feature cycle and confirmed green before the image was rebuilt/retagged. Full round trip live-verified end-to-end against a real backend, real Postgres, real MinIO, and a real spawned container: submit -> claim -> chunked score -> upload -> complete -> presigned result, output byte-exact against a reference using the same softsensor_scaling.to_model_ready /predict itself calls. TWO REAL BUGS FOUND AND FIXED DURING VERIFICATION, not merely designed around: (1) the submit route was POST /predict:batch, which find-my-way (Fastify's router) parses as a param opener rather than a literal colon — it happened to match the literal string but ALSO matched any /predict<suffix>; fixed to /predict-batch. (2) this file's isUniqueViolation (and, discovered but NOT fixed here, its identical copies in model-version.authorized.service.ts and dataset-draft.authorized.service.ts) checked err.meta.target for the P2002 constraint name, but this Prisma version's driver-adapter error shape has no `target` field at all — reproduced live, the constraint name only appears inside meta.driverAdapterError.cause.originalMessage. The 'catch P2002 by constraint name, fall back to the winner's row' pattern this ledger has cited as proven-safe in three places was, in practice, dead code on every one of the OTHER two call sites: a genuine race there currently surfaces a raw 500 instead of the intended graceful fallback / clean 409. Fixed here; flagged as an open follow-up for the other two files, which this feature's scope does not cover. All infra used for live verification (seeded Model/ModelVersion rows, uploaded synthetic SILVER inputs, spawned containers, prediction output objects) was cleaned up after each check — nothing left seeded in the dev database or MinIO.

SECURITY, FOUND 2026-09-14 WHILE BUILDING MODEL-SERVE-001-T10, AND IT IS A CORRECTION TO T09's OWN FIX. images/trainer/app/train.py's top-level exception handler passes a single `str(err)` to TWO sinks on consecutive lines: `_api.log(str(err), 'error')` -> POST /infer-log -> InferenceWindowLog.message, and `_api.report_failure(str(err))` -> POST /infer-complete -> InferenceWindow.failureReason. MODEL-SERVE-001-T09 identified this string as leaking a presigned URL's X-Amz-Signature/X-Amz-Credential (requests' HTTPError embeds the full URL, and pipelines/infer.py downloads both the model and the input by presigned URL) and added lib/redact-urls.ts — but applied it ONLY in getStatusService, i.e. only to the failureReason copy shown on the status card. The identical credential sat unredacted in InferenceWindowLog and was returned raw by `listLogsService`, a committed JwtAccessGuard route, from 2026-09-10 until 2026-09-14. This violates global_definition_of_done item 8 ('no result bytes and no presigned URLs pass through a log') and MODEL-FLOW-000-T06's absolute rule that the URL IS the capability. LESSON, GENERALISED: when a redaction is added because a writer produces dangerous text, find EVERY sink that writer feeds, not the one the bug report happened to arrive through. train.py's two sinks are two lines apart and were missed anyway. A third sink exists and is accepted: api.py mirrors every log line to stderr, so `docker logs` retains the raw text — that is server-side evidence behind an operator boundary, deliberately not redacted, the same split redact-urls.ts's own header states.

MODEL-SERVE-001-T10, 2026-09-14. `InferenceWindow.imageDigest` IS NOT A RELIABLE 'did a container run' SIGNAL, despite its schema comment ('Null until a container is spawned (a SKIPPED window never runs one)') reading exactly like it is. Verified in live Postgres against model TM2: 20 of its 50 FAILED windows carry both a `containerId` and a `startedAt` while `imageDigest` is null — containers that were spawned and then reaped by a server restart before they reached the claim callback. `containerId` is the discriminator; imageDigest is apparently only stamped later in the lifecycle than the comment implies. Any surface that branches on imageDigest to say whether a container ran will be wrong for this whole class of window, and wrong in the reassuring direction ('no container' for one that existed and died). Worth a follow-up: either stamp imageDigest at spawn alongside containerId, or correct the schema comment so the next reader does not repeat this.

MODEL-SERVE-006 DEFECT, found 2026-09-14 during MODEL-SERVE-001-T10's live verification: infer.py's FINAL log line can never be persisted, silently. images/trainer/app/pipelines/infer.py calls `api.complete({...})` at :143 and only THEN `api.log('Inference window complete.')` at :151. But completeService sets `tokenExpiresAt: new Date(0)` on BOTH its SUCCEEDED and FAILED paths, so by the time that log POST is made the window's token is dead, InferenceWindowTokenGuard rejects it, and RunApi.log swallows transport errors by design — no error surfaces anywhere. Confirmed empirically: a successful run wrote exactly 3 of its 4 expected lines, and the image's infer.py was verified byte-identical to the source tree, so this is NOT trainer-image drift. The failure path is unaffected and must stay that way: train.py logs `str(err)` at :66 BEFORE `report_failure` at :67, which is the only reason error text survives at all. FIX IS ONE OF: move the final api.log above api.complete in infer.py, or stop invalidating the token inside completeService and let it lapse on its own TTL. Low severity — one cosmetic line — but it makes every successful window's log look truncated to anyone reading it, which is exactly the sort of thing that gets mistaken for a bug in the reader this task just built.

NEW 2026-09-14 (MODEL-SERVE-001-T11), LIVE-MEASURED AND FIXED. The scheduler dispatched every window one full cadence before its own windowEnd — schema.prisma documents the contract as `windowEnd = now() - lag`, but insertDueWindows computed `to = now - lag` against windowSTART, not windowEnd. At cadence 60 / lag 15 a window became "due" 19 minutes into its own 60-minute span, 42 minutes before its real end, and python passed that future windowEnd straight to PI as endTime. MEASURED, not inferred: 20 fully-elapsed windows (backfilled, materialized once PI was briefly reachable) returned exactly 60/60 rows at 0% missing; the 4 live-dispatched windows returned 19, 19, 20, 30 rows, tracking elapsed minutes almost exactly. Fixed with `to = now - (lag + cadence) * 60_000`, one line, backfillService left untouched (user-supplied range). NEGATIVE CONTROL ACTUALLY RUN: the new dispatch test was executed against the reverted pre-fix line under a fixed clock and observed to FAIL (expected 09:00, received the pre-fix 10:00) before the fix was restored and the suite reconfirmed green — the fix is demonstrated, not merely asserted. A staleness companion was needed and shipped in the same change: the fix moves every window's completion one cadence later, and INFERENCE_STALE_AFTER_CADENCES was computed from windowStart alone in two places (lib/deploy-status.ts and inference-window.authorized.service.ts), so unchanged it would have read a merely-slow, perfectly healthy model as `error`. A shared isStale() helper now accounts for the cadence+lag processing interval before counting staleness cadences, in both places.

NEW 2026-09-14 (MODEL-SERVE-001-T11), DEV-ENVIRONMENT FACT, NOT A CODE DEFECT. INFERENCE_MIN_ROWS=10 was found live in the running backend PROCESS environment (confirmed via `ps eww` on the actual `node dist/main` pid) while existing in NO file anywhere in the repo — not .env, not .env.example, not any shell rc file (~/.zshrc/.zshenv/.zprofile all checked, none reference it). It was set inline in the shell that launched `pnpm dev`. The timing brackets exactly the 06:00 window SKIPping at the real default (30) and the very next 07:00 window SUCCEEDing — meaning two windows (19 rows each, the number T11's fix now corrects for) were scored and their predictions published under a floor a third of the intended size, with no record of the deviation anywhere a later reader could find it. The value reverts to 30 silently on the next clean-shell restart, which is also the point at which T11's own fix makes 30 safe to be reachable again (complete windows now carry 60 rows, not 19-30). The user was asked and chose: report only, they unset it themselves — not something this task could reach from inside the repo.

NEW 2026-09-14 (MODEL-SERVE-001-T12), LIVE-CONFIRMED AND FIXED. points[].features (the Input Data tab's traffic side) is the /predict request's own RAW value, never `scaled` -- apps/serving/services/prediction_log.py's log_prediction builds its ingest body from `rows` (the caller-supplied request); `scaled` feeds ONLY featureStats aggregates. lib/model-input-features.ts nonetheless called inverseScale() on these values as though they were a scaled artifact column. Confirmed to hit the CORRUPTED branch against real data: the pinned model's own feature_spec.json resolves 22 minmax scalingParams entries, and a real FI001.PV reading of ~190 (against its own real min/max 179.72/206.72) would render as ~5,309 -- off by ~28x, labelled "engineering units". The wrong belief was written as fact in THREE separate comments simultaneously (serving, backend, client) before this task, none of which had been cross-checked against the code the others actually described. Fixed: the inversion is removed entirely; a logged value is already engineering units and is now rendered untouched. scalingParams stays on the response for other surfaces (DS-LAKE-025-T06) that DO read a genuinely-scaled value.

features.title: Audit — Replace Every UNVERIFIED Finding With a Fact
features.description: This ledger was written from another ledger, not from the tree. Nothing below MODEL-SERVE-000 should be scoped, estimated or started until these reads are done, because the shape of each downstream feature depends on what is already there. The precedent is direct: MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code and one whose premise was inverted, and the cost of that was a task list nobody could trust.
features.audit_result_2026_09_01: COMPLETED. Re-audited against the tree (schema.prisma, artifact_service.py, feature_spec_service.py, trainning-container.authorized.service.ts, artifact-cleanup.admin.service.ts, dataset.authorized.service.ts), the live dev Postgres (73 ModelTrainingRun rows, 61 SUCCEEDED, 20 Models) and the live dev MinIO (21 feature_spec.json objects). The precedent repeated: this ledger's two highest-severity findings (T03's 'three-hop chain', T07's 'nothing pins or protects') were BOTH wrong in the direction of overstating the gap — both artifact pinning and scaler state already exist and are one hop off the run row. A new, correct highest-severity finding was found in their place: the empty-`scaling` trap (T03). See the corrected findings[] entries and decisions{} above for the full evidence trail; every correction preserves the original claim per V01's rule.

tasks.title: Read run_manifest.json's contents
tasks.detail: NARROWED 2026-08-24 by the MinIO observation — the object exists, is named run_manifest.json, and is 1.2 KiB, so this is no longer 'find out what the trainer uploads' but 'read one known 1.2 KiB file'. Download it and record its literal schema here. The three questions that decide downstream scope: (1) is there a checksum of model.joblib? (2) is the framework and its exact version recorded? (3) does it carry the featureSpecKey of the artifact it was fitted against, or must that be resolved through the run row? If (3) is yes, the three-hop chain collapses to two and MODEL-SERVE-000-T07 shrinks.

tasks.detail: packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma. MODEL-FLOW-010-T08 already caught this ledger's sibling asserting a row held fields it did not, so read the model, do not infer it from MODEL-FLOW-007's task titles. tasks.title: Trace the preprocessing path end to end and decide how serving reuses it
tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: no longer 'trace the whole preprocessing path' — feature_columns is inlined in run_manifest.json, so column selection and order are already recoverable. Scope narrows to scalers alone. CHOOSE THE RUN DELIBERATELY: the observed OLS run has no scalers (target_scaled: false, and a 1.1 KiB model.joblib consistent with a bare estimator), so it cannot answer the question no matter how carefully it is read. Find a run whose dataset applied a scaler and start there.
tasks.detail: apps/python artifact_service.py (select_columns, force_keep_target, the scalers path) and feature_spec_service.py. Answer one question: can a serving process apply the identical transform to raw input by calling the same code, or does something in that path assume a whole parquet frame rather than a handful of rows? The answer decides whether serving is a thin loader or needs an extracted, shared transform module — a difference in kind, not degree. Do NOT plan to reimplement it either way; see the findings.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: PREMISE INVERTED (per findings[]): scaler state is NOT missing. feature_spec.json's `scalingParams` carries the fitted params, ModelTrainingRun.featureSpecKey pins the exact spec (verified non-null on 73/73 runs), and `to_model_ready(..., fitted_params=scaling_params)` already applies a fitted transform without re-fitting, with an existing refuse-rather-than-silently-re-fit guard. ANSWER: call it, not extract it — the existing entry points are object-storage-keyed, which fits MODEL-SERVE-006 directly; a synchronous /predict needs a thin in-memory wrapper. Also surfaced the empty-`scaling`-array trap (new finding) — the real risk in this area, and the opposite of what this task originally worried about.

tasks.title: Determine which existing models are servable at all
tasks.detail: For the artifacts that exist, read feature_spec.json and check derived_from_target. Any model with a non-empty closure needs target history at inference and has a different request contract from one without. This is a fact-finding task, not a design one — but if it turns out MOST real soft-sensor models are in that set, /predict's shape changes and it is much cheaper to know now.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: Measured against all 21 live feature_spec.json objects: 0 of 21 have non-empty derived_from_target, 0 of 21 have target_scaled true, 1 of 21 (the ledger's own most-cited example, b9e25f8d) has zero scalingParams and is unservable without a re-fit — and is already correctly refused by the existing coverage guard. See the new servability-census finding for the full table.

tasks.title: Establish what retains the fitted artifact, and pin it if nothing does
tasks.detail:
OPENED 2026-08-24 from the observation that feature_spec.json is not in the run directory. Read DatasetArtifact's lifecycle: is there any path — a dataset edit, a version supersession, MODEL-FLOW-011's sweep, an admin delete — that can remove or orphan an artifact a ModelTrainingRun points at? Check the artifact's own retention alongside the draft-prefix question MODEL-SERVE-000-T06 asks; they are two objects with one consequence and it is cheaper to answer them in one read.

IF NOTHING RETAINS IT: the fix is upstream at Save Model, not here — MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 should record the artifact id and featureSpecKey on the saved Model so the reference is explicit and greppable, and whatever guards artifact deletion must treat a referencing ModelVersion the way MODEL-FLOW-011-T05 treats an adopted run. Deliverable of THIS task is the finding plus the upstream ticket, not a guard written in the wrong ledger.

DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY COPYING feature_spec.json INTO THE RUN PREFIX. That trades a reference problem for a divergence problem and contradicts the adopt-by-pointer rule MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 states, for the same reason it states it.
tasks.result_2026_09_01: CORRECTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (see findings[]). Pinning already exists on ModelTrainingRun (goldArtifactId/goldObjectKey/artifactChecksum/featureSpecKey). Protection already exists: measured live, 100% of 73 runs (0 GOLD) train against FINAL, which is unconditionally excluded from the cleanup candidate query and predicate. 0 of 61 SUCCEEDED runs point at a missing or reclaimed artifact. TWO REAL, NARROWER EXPOSURES SURVIVE: (1) the FINAL protection is a type exclusion, not a ModelTrainingRun reference check — GOLD/SILVER can still age out 'even if lineage-reachable' per the predicate's own comment, latent but real once any launch path targets a non-FINAL artifact; (2) deleteDatasetService has no reference check at all and can orphan goldArtifactId silently. Both named as upstream tickets (MODEL-FLOW/DS-LAKE), not written here. Also opened decisions.open_question_pin_by_pointer_or_copy_bytes for MODEL-SERVE-001 to resolve.

It is known whether serving can call the existing preprocessing or must have it extracted.
